- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) and forecast is flat or rising slowly, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 2–5% for short-term spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and forecast is rising, model often over-optimistic; cap upward momentum at 1–3% above recent peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.25) and history shows mean-reversion pattern, model often fails to revert; apply slight downward bias (–1–3%) to forecast tail.
- If forecast is flat for 3+ consecutive days with sentiment neutral, true price often drifts downward; add small negative drift (–0.5 to –1.5%) to next 5-day horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp rise followed by collapse, model often overweights early momentum; reduce forecast slope after day 5–7.
- If sentiment history shows repeated +0.20 or higher, model tends to over-forecast; apply 1–3% downward correction to final 5–7 days of forecast.
